about: The named faults of geom-solidcore's tests at the pinned commit of solidcore (decision 32.70): each a test that fails by design, with the one cause of its failure. An SC entry is solidcore's fault: a case of tests/cases.json it answers wrongly. An entry marked ours is not solidcore's: a CK entry is a test the kernel's own checker (geom-check) lacks, a WR entry a limit of geom-solidcore's own interface, each a kernel piece to open. Every test still expects the kernel's answer and fails; kernel.yml's jobs solidcore and solidcore-wasm pass only when the tests that fail are exactly the ones listed here. A fault of solidcore is fixed on the fork's branch, or the operation it blocks stays the kernel's own.

faults.fault: SC-1, two solids 1e-7 apart joined: solidcore's zone tolerance (1e-5) merges faces closer than it
faults.solidcore_gives: one solid of 6 faces and volume 2.0000001000000003
faults.expected: two lumps of 12 faces and volume 2, as the closed form and the kernel's exact geom-bool give
faults.blocks: flat-faced booleans: they stay on the kernel's exact geom-bool

faults.fault: SC-2, solids that do not meet are an error: intersect_breps reports a failed status, not an empty answer
faults.solidcore_gives: the error "the B-reps do not intersect", for two spheres apart
faults.expected: no meeting curve and no point
faults.blocks: meeting two solids (geom-solidcore's meet) for solids apart, nested or concentric

faults.fault: SC-2, solids that do not meet are an error: intersect_breps reports a failed status, not an empty answer
faults.solidcore_gives: the error "the B-reps do not intersect", for one sphere inside the other
faults.expected: no meeting curve and no point
faults.blocks: meeting two solids (geom-solidcore's meet) for solids apart, nested or concentric

faults.fault: SC-2, solids that do not meet are an error: intersect_breps reports a failed status, not an empty answer
faults.solidcore_gives: the error "the B-reps do not intersect", for concentric spheres
faults.expected: no meeting curve and no point
faults.blocks: meeting two solids (geom-solidcore's meet) for solids apart, nested or concentric

faults.fault: SC-3, a wall 1e-7 from another joined into one solid: solidcore's zone tolerance (1e-5) closes the gap between the two walls
faults.solidcore_gives: one solid of volume 4.20000006 (the gap of 1e-7 x 0.2 x 3 filled), 10 faces
faults.expected: two solids of 12 faces and volume 4.2, as the closed form gives
faults.blocks: the union of two solids (geom-solidcore's union) whose faces come closer than 1e-5 without touching: walls, slabs and every flat-faced union stay on the kernel's exact geom-bool

faults.fault: SC-4, a window leaving a sliver of 1e-6 above it loses the sliver: solidcore takes the cutter's top, 1e-6 below the wall's, as the wall's top
faults.solidcore_gives: volume 1.9999999999999993, one solid: the 1e-6 head over the window is gone
faults.expected: volume 2.0000002 (2.4 - 0.2 x 1 x (2 - 1e-6)), one solid with the sliver kept
faults.blocks: the difference of two solids (geom-solidcore's difference) where a face of the cutter comes within 1e-5 of a face of the body: openings in walls and slabs stay on the kernel's exact geom-bool

faults.fault: SC-5, a cylinder's cap off square to its axis: solidcore writes a cap of its cylinder on a plane about 2e-16 off square to the cylinder's axis (the cylinder of radius 0.5 and height 1 on the origin has its top cap's v axis (-1, 0, 2.1410351709324202e-16) and its origin at z = 0.9999999999999999), so the cap and the side do not meet in the one circle they share; group 3 of the kernel's checker certifies a plane and a cylinder meeting only along a shared full circle when the plane is exactly square to the axis, and so refuses the cylinder. The same rows with that one plane square pass (convert.rs, a_cylinder_fails_on_its_top_cap_alone)
faults.solidcore_gives: a cylinder the kernel's checker refuses, its first fault "group 3, face 0: no certified test of this pair exists yet (face 1)"
faults.expected: the case's answer in tests/cases.json, from a cylinder whose caps are square to its axis, as the kernel's geom-make writes its own
faults.blocks: every operation on a cylinder made by solidcore (geom-solidcore's cylinder, and the sections and booleans of one). Behind it (a diagnostic run with the caps written square, not committed), isect-21 to isect-27, isect-40, isect-41 and results_are_the_kernels_bodies pass, and the booleans of bool-22, bool-23, bool-24, bool-27, bldg-12, bldg-14, bldg-15, bldg-24, bldg-28 and bldg-29 meet unchecked pairs of group 3 (CK-2)

faults.fault: SC-5, a cylinder's cap off square to its axis: solidcore writes a cap of its cylinder on a plane about 2e-16 off square to the cylinder's axis (the cylinder of radius 0.5 and height 1 on the origin has its top cap's v axis (-1, 0, 2.1410351709324202e-16) and its origin at z = 0.9999999999999999), so the cap and the side do not meet in the one circle they share; group 3 of the kernel's checker certifies a plane and a cylinder meeting only along a shared full circle when the plane is exactly square to the axis, and so refuses the cylinder. The same rows with that one plane square pass (convert.rs, a_cylinder_fails_on_its_top_cap_alone)
